title: Stochastic and quantum autonomous information machine: efficiency fluctuations, precision and optimization
abstract: We investigate the conversion between thermal and informational resources in an autonomous machine coupled to thermal reservoirs and a tape, playing the role of an information reservoir. The machine is able to perform information erasure driven by heat, and information-powered refrigeration, for which we introduce suitable efficiency definitions. We focus on the role of fluctuations in the currents and stochastic efficiencies, as well as in operation at optimal performance. The model is also extended to allow a coherent information reservoir, which is able to modify operation and performance. All in all, our work provides insights for the design and optimization of information-to-work conversion devices at small scales.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to study how information can be used as a resource to drive energy conversion in small-scale machines. By analyzing stochastic fluctuations and defining information-based efficiencies, the authors derive fundamental thermodynamic bounds governing the trade-off between precision and energy dissipation. This has implications for designing highly efficient, information-aware nanoscale devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental limits and dynamics of converting between thermal energy and information resources in an autonomous machine.
main_result: It establishes quantitative bounds (like the TUR) on the trade-off between the precision of energy extraction and the associated dissipation, particularly highlighting the role of stochastic fluctuations.
method: The analysis employs non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) theory, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics applied to a quantum master equation framework.
model_or_system: The model is an autonomous machine (two-level subsystems A and B) coupled to two thermal baths (hot/cold) and an information reservoir modeled as a bit-tape. The dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating thermal jumps and information-driven transitions.
key_observables: Stationary thermodynamic currents ($\dot{Q}_c, \dot{Q}_h$), entropy change ($\dot{S}_{	ext{tape}}$), and their associated variance rates ($	ext{Var}[\dot{Q}]$).
important_parameters: The information bias ($\delta_{	ext{tape}}$) and the thermal bias ($\delta_{	ext{th}}$) are key parameters determining the operational regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the tape bits are energetically degenerate and that the interaction with the tape occurs at Poisson-distributed times.
figures_summary: Figures sketch the informational machine setup, show the state diagram, and illustrate the transitions driven by bit flips on the tape.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by first defining the dynamics, then calculating stationary currents, investigating fluctuation theorems (TUR), and finally exploring different operational regimes (e.g., erasure, refrigeration).
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative framework for analyzing non-equilibrium thermodynamics in systems where information processing is coupled to energy exchange, which is highly relevant for understanding nanoscale energy conversion devices.
